structure_pass_disagreement.key_disagreement_R12_vs_R1: An ambiguous criterion set, not a judgment error. Neither R12 ("does one job ... split test") nor R1 ("no speculative capability, tool grant, or frontmatter field beyond what the remit requires") describes 'the remit is delegated to fetched content'; that defect is A26/F1, which belong to Pass 2. The structure pass has no criterion for an open remit driven by fetched content, so each run attached the nearest structure-pass key — R12 via 'scope', R1 via 'Bash beyond the remit'. Both arms' own text concedes the overlap (gated: "the detail sweep would probably also raise ... `A26` and group `F`. Treat that as the same defect"; forced: "The detail pass should also score A26 and A10 on this same line"). Fix belongs to the checklist: either give A26 a structure-pass companion or say which structure key owns an open remit.
structure_pass_disagreement.tier_disagreement_A1: Primarily sampling variance on a permissive criterion. A1's own text supports High: "This can be a High finding, because a subagent that should have been a skill hides every intermediate step from the user who wanted to see them", and the forced arm's own Manifests scenario (store and mirror emptied and compacted before the user learns of it) is concrete and safety-breaking, which the scale defines as High. The forced arm's Medium rests on (a) "can be" being permissive rather than mandatory and (b) low confidence that the form is wrong — but the scale maps confidence to a separate axis, not to tier, and the demotion rule demotes only when the scenario cannot be stated concretely. The fixture and A1's text therefore support the gated arm's High better. Contributing factor: the forced arm's structure spawn prompt carried the focus note "the user pre-authorized the full detail sweep regardless of the gate", which may have lowered the stakes of the tier call; thinking blocks are redacted so this cannot be confirmed.
